nv_den_of_thieves_area.blurb: Den of Thieves is a small limestone sport wall high on Mount Charleston in the Spring Mountains, set slightly apart from the rest of Robber's Roost. Thirteen bolted routes cover a wide spread, from a handful of easy and moderate lines up to a cluster of 5.11s that make up the bulk of the wall. The face is a clean, slabby, bluish-grey sheet that looks away from the afternoon sun, so it stays cool and is a good choice for hot summer days when the valley below is baking. Expect company at the neighbouring walls, since the whole canyon draws steady crowds, including hikers.

nv_dog_wall.blurb: Dog Wall is a short sandstone wall in the Calico Hills of Red Rock Canyon, tucked into a small side gully near the first parking area. It holds a dozen routes, a mix of sport and trad lines with one boulder problem, running from an easy 5.6 range up through the 5.10s and 5.11s to a couple of 5.12s. Its southeast-facing position makes it a reasonable pick for cold days, though it keeps shade longer in the morning during spring. Because the walk from the car is so short, sightseers often wander past, so expect an audience.

nv_little_springs_crag.blurb: Little Springs Crag sits in a drainage at the south side of the Ash Creek area in Calico Basin, on red Calico Hills sandstone. A dozen sport and trad routes are split between a small lower tier and a bigger upper tier. The sport lines tend to be technical slab climbs, while the trad lines follow chimneys and wide cracks. Most grades fall in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, with an easy route or two at the bottom end and a single 5.12 at the top. It catches early sun and then sits mostly in shade, making it a decent warm-weather afternoon option away from the busier crags.

nv_the_trophy_wall.blurb: The Trophy Wall is a small, steep amphitheatre of pale sandstone in the northern part of Sandstone Quarry in Red Rock Canyon. Every route is bolted, and all of them sit in the hard end of the sport spectrum: seven at 5.12 and five at 5.13, with nothing easier. Expect sustained, pumpy climbing on steep rock. The wall catches sun until late in the day, and the gully funnels wind, so it can feel breezy even when it is warm. The hike in follows a trail for about twenty minutes with a fair amount of uphill.

nv_front_bouldering_wall.blurb: Front Bouldering Wall is a compact cliff of about thirty feet, on the right just inside the mouth of Lower Canyon in Keyhole Canyon, in the Eldorado Mountains south of Las Vegas. The quartz monzonite is varnished and small-grained, and the climbing feels balancy and slippery. Most of the dozen climbs are boulder problems from VB up to about V4, with a few trad and top-rope lines from 5.8 into the 5.10s and one harder at 5.12. There are no bolts, so top-rope anchors are built from gear. Highball problems on mostly decent landings are the draw. The canyon is remote and quiet.

nv_ranch_hands_crag.blurb: Ranch Hands Crag is a sandstone wall in the Red Spring part of Calico Basin, in Red Rock Canyon. It holds a dozen routes, mostly bolted, plus a single trad line and one top-rope line. The sport routes are steady and fairly hard, with a couple at 5.10, a handful at 5.11 and several at 5.12, and one very easy route. The left side faces east for morning sun and afternoon shade, while the right side faces northeast and goes shady early. The crag is easy to reach but overshadowed by the nearby Cannibal Crag, so it is generally quieter.
